title: These Are Best Stocks to Buy After Earnings
creator: Daniel Pronk
summary: Daniel Pronk's 5 November 2026 rapid-fire earnings roundup covers seven stocks that collapsed after reporting - Palantir, Shopify, Intel, Reddit, Fortinet, ServiceNow and Uber - and he buys none of them. His recurring theme is deceleration killing multiples: Palantir posted a 'ridiculous' quarter ($2bn revenue, Rule of 40 score of 158%, $10.4bn cash, no debt) but total contract value grew only 6% and at 101x free cash flow he stays out; Shopify grew revenue 32% with a near-perfect growth chart yet 83x FCF yields only a 9% CAGR in his DCF; Intel beat Q3 but guided Q4 revenue down, and at 81x FCF he calls it a low-quality chip stock he would not own at any price. Reddit looks cheap at 19x FCF after a 53% revenue quarter, but US daily actives fell 2% and Google's AI summaries are draining ~1m search referrals a week, so he lacks confidence. Fortinet (27x FCF) and ServiceNow (~24x FCF) are both decelerating with compressing margins - ServiceNow also faces accelerating stock-based compensation and what he calls an over-promotional CEO. Uber is the cheapest of the group at 16x forward earnings with 20% bookings growth, but autonomous-driving uncertainty keeps him out. He closes by noting Mercado Libre, a large existing holding, reports after hours. Caption garbles: several figures are missing entirely (Palantir's net revenue retention, its US commercial growth rate, ServiceNow's RPO guide percentage, Reddit's US ARPU growth figure), and 'dank strong' is a garble of 'strong.'

calls.thesis: Incredible quarter (Q3 revenue $2bn, Rule of 40 score 158%, $10.4bn cash, zero debt) but the multiple demands near-impossible sustained growth; total contract value only +6% YoY signals deceleration.
calls.price_at_call: 101x free cash flow; no share price stated; down ~19% over the past month

calls.thesis: Great business, beautiful growth (29% GMV, 32% revenue, FCF $2.7bn TTM) but 83x FCF is too high a price; DCF of 30% FCF growth at 50x FCF yields only a 9% CAGR, and the multiple will contract as growth decelerates.
calls.price_at_call: 83x free cash flow; no share price stated; down 21% from recent highs

calls.thesis: Q3 revenue +21% to $16.5bn was solid and FCF is positive again ($3bn YTD), but the Q4 guide implies a sequential revenue decline, operating income/cash flow remain far below all-time highs; one of the lowest-quality chip stocks - not interested 'at any price.'
calls.price_at_call: 81x free cash flow, 43x forward P/E; no share price stated; down 60% from all-time highs, 50% in the last month

calls.thesis: Revenue +20%, product revenue +37%, billings +29% is good, but growth is decelerating (Q4 guide +17.8%, analysts expect sub-10% by end-2027) and 27x FCF is still too high for a slowing business.
calls.price_at_call: 27x free cash flow (was ~40x before earnings); no share price stated; down 35% from recent highs

calls.thesis: Decent quarter (revenue +21%) but RPO growth decelerating to 18.5%, gross margins down 3% YoY and falling for ~18 months, operating margins down to 9.7% from ~14%, stock-based compensation accelerating while fundamentals don't, and a CEO he calls too promotional about AI tailwinds that aren't materialising.
calls.price_at_call: ~24x free cash flow; no share price stated; down 31% after earnings

calls.thesis: Actually cheap for a business growing bookings 20%+ with five straight quarters above 20% bookings growth - but he is not a buyer because he doesn't know what the business looks like long-term as autonomous driving (Waymo, Tesla) becomes mainstream, and he only takes concentrated, high-conviction positions.
calls.price_at_call: 16x forward P/E, ~14.6x free cash flow; no share price stated; down ~28% from all-time highs, up 7% on the day after earnings
